context: Prep note for my one-to-one with my manager Rina Cole. My goals: ask for a raise, ask to lead the migration project. My achievements this quarter: 4 of 5 goals delivered, page load time cut by 40 percent, mentored one new colleague. Workload: two projects and about 50 hour weeks. Promotion cycle starts in March. The migration project starts in April. Things I want to hear: what promotion needs, when the budget decision is made.

lines.text: Hi Rina, thanks for making time. How was your week?

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Busy but good. Thanks for the notes you sent before. Let us start with how you feel about the quarter.
I feel good about it overall. I delivered most of my goals.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: I looked at the tracker and I count three of five goals done.
I have four of five, I think the tracker missed the search goal.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Possibly. I will check it again. What did you ship that you are proud of?
I cut the page load time by forty percent, and I mentored a new colleague.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Nice. How is your workload right now? You looked tired in the last meeting.
It is heavy. I have two projects at once and my weeks are around fifty hours.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: That is more than I knew. We should fix that.
Thank you. That brings me to something I wanted to ask. I would like to talk about a raise.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: I understand. Honestly, this is not the right time, we are in a budget freeze until next quarter.
I get that. What would I need to show, and when does the freeze end?

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: I cannot give a date. The decision is made by the finance team in a calibration meeting.
Okay. And what would the promotion require from me?

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: That is a bigger conversation. Let me think about how to answer it properly.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Let me ask you something else. What do you need from me to be more effective?
I need clear priorities between the two projects and fewer meetings.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: That is fair. Also, we need one extra person on the on-call rotation. Would you take one extra week a month?
Before I agree, I want to see how that fits with my current workload.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Fair. The migration project would start in May, by the way.
I had April in my notes, can we confirm the month?

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: I will confirm it. Also, I wonder whether you plan to stay with us for the long term.
Yes, I want to grow here, and the migration role matters to me.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Separate topic. One of your teammates told me there is tension between you and Omar.
I would like to hear what exactly was said before I respond.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: I do not want to name names. Just try to talk to him this week.
Okay, I will talk to him.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Sorry, one moment, my phone is ringing. Let me silence it.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Okay. The new coffee machine is finally installed, did you try it?
Not yet, but I heard it is much better.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: It is. The old one was terrible.
Agreed.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Dan, can you send me the tracker export?
Sure, I will send it after our meeting.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Now, what do you want from the next year?
I want to lead the migration project and work toward a promotion.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: I like the migration idea. I will talk to HR about it by Friday.
Thank you. And I will write a summary of my achievements by Monday.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Good. That will help me argue for you.
Before we finish, I still do not know what the promotion needs. Could we come back to that?

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Fair. Let us set a slot next week to go through the criteria.
Great. Thank you, Rina.

lines.speaker: Rina
lines.text: Thank you Dan.
